subject: Clarify: default retention windows, residency, and erasure evidence
messages:

Subject: Clarify: default retention windows, residency, and erasure evidence

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked us to get a concise answer set on a few items before we move ahead:

1) For the hosted Redwood API, what are the default retention windows for: (a) raw requests/prompts (including streaming fragments), (b) model-generated responses/final outputs, and (c) embeddings/derived artifacts?
2) Where are those artifacts stored by default (US/EU region) and can we require residency in a specific region?
3) If we need a complete account-level erasure (data subject request / procurement requirement), what's your process, how long does it take, and what evidence do you provide back to us?
4) Do attachments uploaded in requests (files referenced by the request) count differently for retention?

We need short, definitive answers for our procurement/security team (they prefer bullets). If you have a short matrix or one-pager, attach it.

Appreciate it — Amelia

Amelia Rios
Head of Security Operations, FinHealth

Hi Amelia —

Thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise, procurement-friendly summary. I'm including Karthik (runtime) and will loop in Kim (policy) with a short matrix and evidence notes attached.

One-line summary (hosted Redwood API, default settings):
- Raw requests / prompts (including transient stream fragments): retained by default for 30 days and then removed from customer-accessible stores; short-lived kernel caches are ephemeral (24 hours) and not considered part of the retention window.
- Model-generated responses / final outputs: retained by default for 90 days. These are the artifacts used for debugging, quality monitoring, and regression evals unless you opt-out.
- Embeddings & derived artifacts: retained by default for 90 days; embeddings used for indexing can be configured separately and may be stored longer when explicitly enabled.

Residency and region behavior:
- Default storage region is the region you select at account creation (e.g., us-west or eu-west). For hosted accounts we do not replicate across regions by default.
- You can require residency in a specific region via a configuration flag (we'll enforce at the tenancy level). Dedicated/Private deployments provide stronger guarantees and contractual residency controls.

Erasure / account-level deletion process and evidence:
- Request intake: Submit an erasure request via our Portal (or HubSpot ticket HS-89273).
- Execution: Our ops team runs the deletion job across active stores and index shards. Standard timeline: 5 business days for primary stores; up to 30 calendar days for full propagation (backups/replication/long-term snapshots).
- Evidence: We provide an audit package that includes the deletion job run-id, timestamps, and a verification report. For SOC2/Procurement you can get a signed deletion certificate and a log export showing the job completion.

Attachments in requests:
- Files uploaded as part of a request are treated as request artifacts and follow the same default windows as raw requests (30 days). If you ingest files into an index or embeddings pipeline, those derived artifacts follow the embeddings retention rules (90 days by default) unless you configure otherwise.

Notes & options:
- You can shorten all default windows at the account level or for specific routes via the Console (session retainments, auto-purge rules).
- For regulated customers we recommend Dedicated or Private (VPC) deployment to get contractual residency and stricter retention windows.

I'm attaching a short matrix (see retention_matrix_v2.xlsx) that lays this out with examples. Kim will follow up with notes about legal evidence for erasure and exceptions.

Next action: If this covers your needs I can convert to a one-page statement for procurement.

Best,

- For the deletion evidence: will the deletion certificate include checksums or hash references we can reconcile against data we supplied?

Hi Amelia — quick answers and we've attached a concise one-pager (Retention_Summary_FinHealth_v1.pdf) and the matrix Marissa mentioned.

1) PII in model outputs:
- Policy: We treat stored artifacts the same regardless of content class. If a customer identifies PII in a stored artifact and requests erasure, we will remove the artifact under the standard erasure process.
- Expedited flow: We offer an expedited erasure SLA for PII-marked items (72 hours) when requested via the Portal with an elevated priority code (used for data-subject erasure requests). The expedited flow skips non-essential manual review steps and prioritizes the deletion job across shards.

2) Deletion evidence and reconciliation:
- The audit package includes: deletion_job_id, per-shard timestamps, and object identifiers. We can include object-level identifiers that are a salted hash of the original request id + truncated hash of the payload so you can reconcile without us sharing raw content.
- Checksums: we do not return raw content checksums by default (security reasons), but we can include HMAC-style artifacts for reconciliation under an NDA.

3) Console "reduce retention" behavior:
- When you reduce retention at the account/route level, it applies to new and existing artifacts that are still within the previous retention window. That means previously retained debug artifacts older than the new target will be scheduled for purge according to the new rule (subject to backup propagation windows).
- Note: historical aggregates and anonymized telemetry used solely for platform health are pre-aggregated and retained under a separate policy; that telemetry is not reversible on a per-customer basis.

Other operational notes:
- Backups: full snapshots may persist longer; purge from backups can take up to 30 days to fully propagate.
- Contractual options: For enterprise contracts we include specific deletion SLAs and stronger proof artifacts in the Private/Dedicated offerings.

I've attached the two files and added the HubSpot ticket reference. If you'd like, we can convert the matrix into the language procurement prefers and add to the MSA as a data-retention rider.

Cheers,
